title: Hybrid Work Stipend, Ergonomics & Home Office Procurement Guidelines
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This page documents Redwood Inference’s policy and operational playbook for hybrid work stipends, ergonomics support, and home-office procurement. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, new hires, and individual contributors who work from a home or remote location at least part of the week. The goal is to ensure a consistent, safe, and equitable program that supports employee wellbeing and productivity while keeping procurement and cost control straightforward.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees and eligible contractors on assignments longer than 6 months.
- Covers one-time home-office stipend, an annual refresh window, and an ergonomics assessment/approved equipment replacement policy.
- Does not replace team-provided standing desks or on-site furniture budgets for office locations.

Key principles

- Equity: All eligible employees receive clear, predictable support regardless of role or seniority level.
- Safety and comfort: Ergonomic equipment that prevents injury takes priority over decorative purchases.
- Simplicity: Purchasing and reimbursement workflows use existing tools (IT Asset Portal, Ramp, Jira Service Desk) and minimize ad-hoc approvals.
- Auditability: All purchases are tracked and coded for finance and audit purposes.

Eligibility and amounts

- New full-time hires: One-time onboarding stipend of $650 to be used for home office setup. This is payable after start date and is disbursed as a taxable stipend on payroll (default) or via Ramp virtual card on request.
- Existing employees: Annual refresh stipend of $300 every January (pro-rated in the first calendar year if hire/transfer occurs after July 1).
- Ergonomics escalation: Up to $1,200 available (separate from stipends) for medically necessary ergonomic equipment recommended by Redward’s approved occupational health vendors and approved by People Ops.

Stipend table (overview)

| Item | Eligibility | Amount | Frequency | Routing |
|------|-------------|--------|-----------|---------|
| Onboarding stipend | New FT hire or transfer | $650 | One-time | Payroll or Ramp |
| Annual refresh | All FT employees | $300 | Annually (Jan) | Payroll credit or Ramp |
| Ergonomics equipment | Medically recommended | Up to $1,200 | As needed, needs approval | People Ops approval + procurement route |

Acceptable purchases

- Approved: monitors, monitor arms, ISO keyboards, ergonomic mice, monitor stands, chairs (when ergonomics approved), external webcams, headsets, surge-protected power strips, docking stations, and lighting that improves video meeting visibility.
- Not approved: consumer art, subscriptions (streaming), food, plants, decorative-only items, multi-monitor stands > 3 monitors without documented need, or uncertified used equipment unless approved by IT for security.

Request and procurement workflows

1) Quick-buy (preferred small purchases, < $300):
   - Employee uses Ramp virtual card or personal card and submits receipt in Ramp/Expensify within 14 days.
   - Expense should be tagged: GL code BEN-HOME-OFFICE.
   - Manager auto-approves; People Ops receives an FYI.

2) Guided-buy (> $300 and <= stipend amount):
   - Employee creates a short request in the IT Asset Portal (portal.redwood.internal -> Home Office Requests) including a short justification and 1–2 vendor links.
   - IT/Procurement will validate compatibility (security/ports/warranty) within 2 business days and approve or suggest alternatives.
   - Approved purchases are issued on a Ramp card or via direct procurement by IT.

3) Ergonomics escalation (potentially > $1,200):
   - Complete the ergonomics screening form (link in the portal). If the screening indicates elevated risk or need, People Ops coordinates a vendor evaluation (Redwood uses Occupational Health Partner: KineticHealth).
   - If a vendor recommends equipment, People Ops submits a procurement approval request to Finance.

Onboarding provisioning timeline (recommended)

- Day 0–3: Offer acceptance — People Ops reminds candidate of stipend options in the pre-boarding packet.
- Day 1–7: New hire indicates preferred routing (payroll or Ramp card) in Workday profile or via the IT Asset Portal.
- Day 7–21: First Ramp disbursement or payroll stipend delivered. Employee may request guided-buy items in the same window; IT aims to approve within 2 business days.
- Day 30: Manager check-in to confirm setup and identify additional needs.

Roles and ownership

- People Ops: policy owner, approves ergonomics fund disbursements >$1,200, manages tax reporting for payroll stipends, and coordinates vendor relationships.
- IT / Asset Team: compatibility checks, warranty vetting, issuing Ramp cards or physical asset procurement, and inventory tracking.
- Finance: coding, audit, reconciliation, and exceptions approval for atypical purchases.
- Manager: first-line approver for stipend usage, confirms business justification for items that exceed typical amounts.

Tools and integration points

- Ramp: primary corporate card for purchases and receipt ingestion. Use Ramp merchant controls to restrict high-risk categories.
- Workday: source of truth for eligibility and payroll stipend processing.
- IT Asset Portal (Jira Service Desk): ticketing flow for guided-buy and ergonomics requests. Ticket prefix: IT-HOME.
- Confluence: policy and FAQ; link receipts to ticket for audit.

Reimbursement and tax treatment

- Default delivery for the one-time stipend is payroll (taxable income). Employees who prefer Ramp disbursement must opt-in via Workday before the first payroll cycle after hire.
- Small reimbursements (< $300) paid by employee and submitted through Ramp/Expensify will be reimbursed net of payroll taxes (as applicable). People Ops coordinates with Payroll to ensure correct FICA/withholding.

Security and data sanitization

- IT must validate any purchase that includes embedded storage (e.g., refurbished devices, kiosks) for secure wipe policies.
- Employees must follow the IT decommissioning process when disposing of corporate equipment: create an IT ticket and coordinate secure pickup or drop-off.

Exceptions and special cases

- Relocation / country-specific compliance: Amounts and tax treatment may vary by country. Local People Ops leads will publish country addenda (e.g., EU vs US payroll handling).
- Contractors: Eligibility is determined at hire; contract must explicitly list stipend eligibility and routing.
- High-cost accommodations (standing desk + specialized chair > $2,000): require director-level signoff and People Ops + Finance approval.

Audit, reporting, and KPIs

- Quarterly report: People Ops + Finance publish a quarterly home-office spend summary to the exec dashboard (metric examples: number of stipends issued, median spend, ergonomics escalations, time-to-procure).
- Audit cadence: internal audit spot-checks of 10% of purchases annually. Discrepancies are remediated through reclaim or payroll adjustments.

FAQ (selected)

Q: Can I split my stipend across multiple purchases?
A: Yes. Keep receipts and itemize in the expense system. Total reimbursed/stipend usage cannot exceed your eligible amount in a 12-month window.

Q: I need a monitor arm and a lumbar-support chair; how do I request ergonomics approval?
A: Start with the IT Asset Portal ergonomic screening form. If screening indicates elevated risk, People Ops coordinates an occupational health evaluation.

Q: I moved internationally. Do I still get the annual refresh?
A: Eligibility depends on local payroll rules. Contact your local People Ops partner to confirm.
